note.backdrop: At midday Friday the S&P 500 fund is -2.0%, the Nasdaq 100 fund -3.7%, the Russell 2000 fund -1.8% and the VIX +8.6%; the check flagged a market-wide move, so every range is likely too narrow until the next scan, and it did not flag rising fear. The morning's catch-up became a deeper fall in the US session: at 11:02 a.m. ET the Nasdaq 100 fund was about 8.0% below last Friday's close, AMD -10.0% and Micron -11.3% (StockTitan), and by the check the median chip stock was -9.6%. Treasuries keep rising (the 10-year yield -0.12 pt, 4.94% at 17:25Z) while gold (-4.2%) and bitcoin (-4.7%) fall. Consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 from 48.0, and the University of Michigan's survey director tied weaker finances among the largest stockholders to 'continued AI-related agitation in stock markets' (StockTitan). Anthropic was -11.4% at 11:02 a.m. ET (StockTitan). Health insurers had their day without a fall: UnitedHealth $344.54, +4.25% on Thursday's close. A seventh S&P 500 loss in a row is now likely unless the afternoon turns; the close decides it.

themes.beneath: In proportion: the desk's size calls are past their lines by midday against Nov 13's closes: Nvidia $135.47, -16.84% (line 7.5%); AMD $433.92, -18.57% (line 9%); Dell $279.86, -18.40% (line 9.5%). The fall is not in proportion to any one company's news; only Broadcom has some. My inference: Asia's selling on Friday turned into US selling of the whole chain, deeper than the morning's catch-up, as holders cut AI hardware as one position. Over the year the market alone carries about half of these moves (Arista: -4.9% of -11.2%), so the rest is the group.
themes.cause: The semiconductor median is -9.6% (59 stocks), printed circuit boards -9.1%, chip equipment -8.8%, test instruments -8.5%, communications equipment -7.8%. Outside their 9-in-10 ranges: Broadcom -10.7%, Arista -11.2%, Celestica -14.9%; beside them Coherent -14.9%, Applied Optoelectronics -16.1%, Onto -13.9%, TTM -14.4%, Monolithic Power -10.3%. Since this morning AMD went from -6.3% to -11.8% and Micron from -5.0% to -12.6%.
themes.mechanism: One chain, one buyer: these companies sell into the same AI data-center build, and over the year they moved together (Arista with Celestica, Broadcom with Celestica, Coherent with Applied Optoelectronics), so a doubt about the build reaches each at once. Broadcom also has news of its own: Google reportedly cut its planned 2027 shipments of Broadcom-designed AI chips and is preparing to use more MediaTek chips (Investing.com), and Redburn downgraded it.
